paper.title: Motion-Omni: End-to-End Joint Speech and Full-Body Motion for Spoken Dialogue
paper.abstract: An avatar that holds a conversation has to decide what to say and to move while saying it, but these two abilities come from separate families of models: spoken dialogue models return speech but no motion, while co-speech motion models return motion but depend on audio supplied to them rather than deciding what to say. We call a model that produces both from one shared context a spoken motion model, and throughout use motion for co-speech communicative motion: facial expression together with hand, upper-body and lower-body movement. We present Motion-Omni, an end-to-end spoken motion framework with three contributions: (i) a unified architecture (Speech Projector, LLM, Speech Generator, Part-Aware Motion Generator) and a four-stage joint training paradigm that co-adapts all components end-to-end; (ii) a model-agnostic data construction pipeline that produces 422,856 pseudo-labeled speech-motion training samples (1,402 hours) from a reusable motion teacher and a dual-metric quality curriculum; and (iii) a reproducible evaluation setup for this task class, comprising an external conversational prompt set (SwDA-500), matched-audio cascade baselines, and a shared rendering and lip-sync pipeline. Instantiated as Motion-Omni-Q7 with a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backbone, the model reaches 2.62% word error rate, the lowest among the omni-modal systems in our speech comparison, and obtains the best beat correlation and diversity among systems that do not run the motion teacher at inference time. It completes speech-and-motion responses 5.4× faster than the matched non-streaming cascade built from the same speech and motion components.

speech.caption: Speech intelligibility: WER (%) on Seed-TTS-Eval (English split, 1,088 samples); lower is better. Dedicated TTS systems synthesise a supplied sentence, whereas omni-modal LLMs also plan the response.

motion.caption: Motion, facial geometry and lip-sync metrics on SwDA-500. Teacher-referenced metrics compare against LOM-generated motion and therefore favour systems that run LOM at inference time. FGD, BC and BC-bi are in x10<sup>-1</sup> units; Diversity is unscaled.

latency.caption: Response latency on SwDA-500 (non-streaming, full-utterance generation). Slowdown is relative to our model.

paper.arch_caption: Motion-Omni framework with four components and their conditioning topology.
paper.ql_caption: Motion quality against response latency on SwDA-500. Circles are two-stage cascades; the star is our end-to-end model. Points closer to the top-left are better. The dashed line marks RTF = 1, below which a system responds faster than real time.
